newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Camacho forms political party for 2000.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Camacho forms political party for 2000.

text.p: Manuel Camacho Solis, one of Mexico's most controversial politicans, on Thursday announced the formation of a centrist political party but he said it would not take part in mid-term elections in July.

Camacho, once a star protege of ex-President Carlos Salinas until he virtually precipitated a political crisis in 1994, said his Party of the Democratic Centre would set its sights on success in the presidential elections of 2000.

He said it would work with the opposition, and, according to state news agency Notimex, he also left open the door to cooperation with the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) that has ruled Mexico for 67 years.
His party was launched with just a handful of members, Camacho said. His support among many Mexicans is no longer believed to be strong.

Camacho, a former mayor of Mexico City and foreign minister, drove Mexico to the brink of crisis in 1994 when he threatened to challenge Salinas's hand-picked presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio in general elections.
Openly disappointed at not being selected by Salinas, he became the first high-ranking PRI supporter to publicly consider launching a bid for the presidency against the wishes of the incumbent.
Just before Colosio was assasinated in March 1994, Camacho dropped his presidential bid, but he had already lost much support in the ruling party, as well as Salinas's friendship.
He has kept a low profile since.
